models.section: Transmitter, receiver, and final loss integration
models.summary: MU-A-2018-76271-001: A 100 W source, two antenna gains, receiver sensitivity, and signed losses form the budget that is reevaluated after each hop.
MU-A-2018-76271-002: Earth radius, lower-boundary height, and elevation determine the entry angle and straight-leg length.
MU-A-2018-76271-003: A NASA IRI snapshot on a latitude-longitude-altitude grid is linearly interpolated along each ray.
MU-A-2018-76271-004: The printed refractive relation feeds an altitude integral for the entry-to-exit angular sweep.
MU-A-2018-76271-005: A polar parameterization is converted to Cartesian coordinates and integrated between entry and exit.
MU-A-2018-76271-006: Straight and curved segments give B; great-circle forward equations update the global landing point.
MU-A-2018-76271-007: One-hop length feeds free-space loss; the curved segment and plasma state feed absorption.
MU-A-2018-76271-008: Flat land, SRTM mountain patches, calm waves, and rough waves are normalized to small meshes for common reflection calculations.
MU-A-2018-76271-009: The height standard deviation, incidence angle, and wavelength yield a phase term and exponential coherent-amplitude factor.
MU-A-2018-76271-010: Conductivity and relative permittivity determine a complex reflection coefficient, which is combined with the roughness factor.
MU-A-2018-76271-011: Local normals and incident vectors yield reflected vectors; invalid downward vectors are removed and components averaged.
MU-A-2018-76271-012: Each hop updates location, direction, losses, power, and bounce count, producing a terminal path record.

task_reconstruction.decision: Choose configurations and circumstances under which a ray is likely to return with adequate margin, while distinguishing concentrated first-bounce regions from dispersed or failed paths.
inputs: transmitter location, bearing, elevation, frequency, power, antenna gains
terrain, water, power, solar-activity, and coastal scenarios
task_reconstruction.objective: Model multi-hop HF skywave propagation across a spherical Earth with spatially varying ionosphere and multiple land/water reflection surfaces, then translate path survival into ship-reception ranges and operating guidance.
outputs: trajectory, losses, received power, termination class
hop count, surface distance, landing locations
terrain contrasts, parameter working ridge, coastal distance envelopes

unresolved_questions.summary: Every page has a commercial/template watermark; the PDF has 31 physical pages while internal numbering says 30.
Symbols and units conflict with formulas: k, ell/A, Theta prime/Theta_j, tt/G, B, and D are not consistently bound.
The model-construction section states 2001-01-01 01:30 GMT, while Part I and the solar-activity comparison state 2000-01-01.
Equation 10 has dimensional and constant-definition defects that prevent independent reproduction of the trajectory.
Turning-height solution, integration step, no-real-root escape branch, and z(alpha) are missing.
Positive path-loss magnitudes are added in Equation 22 despite Equation 2 describing L as a negative term.
Collision-frequency source, path averaging, and SI/km conversion are absent.
A 10 by 10 m patch is smaller than the roughly 100 m wavelength at 3 MHz and lacks a Fresnel-footprint justification.
A 50 by 50 SRTM subset is horizontally compressed to 10 m, altering slopes and correlation scales.
The Fresnel model assumes perpendicular polarization while the paper says the signal has no assigned polarization.
Equation 19 does not use an explicit complex magnitude squared before the logarithm.
Unweighted averaging of local vectors and a negative-z filter do not establish shadowing or conserved reflected energy.

weaknesses.summary: Every page has a commercial/template watermark; the PDF has 31 physical pages while internal numbering says 30.
Symbols and units conflict with formulas: k, ell/A, Theta prime/Theta_j, tt/G, B, and D are not consistently bound.
The model-construction section states 2001-01-01 01:30 GMT, while Part I and the solar-activity comparison state 2000-01-01.
Equation 10 has dimensional and constant-definition defects that prevent independent reproduction of the trajectory.
Turning-height solution, integration step, no-real-root escape branch, and z(alpha) are missing.
Positive path-loss magnitudes are added in Equation 22 despite Equation 2 describing L as a negative term.
Collision-frequency source, path averaging, and SI/km conversion are absent.
A 10 by 10 m patch is smaller than the roughly 100 m wavelength at 3 MHz and lacks a Fresnel-footprint justification.
A 50 by 50 SRTM subset is horizontally compressed to 10 m, altering slopes and correlation scales.
The Fresnel model assumes perpendicular polarization while the paper says the signal has no assigned polarization.
Equation 19 does not use an explicit complex magnitude squared before the logarithm.
Unweighted averaging of local vectors and a negative-z filter do not establish shadowing or conserved reflected energy.
The 170/180 dB ledger does not include cables, receiver noise, bandwidth, BER, or a numerical component trace.
Calm water uses 10000 rays and turbulent water 1000, with no retained effective n after escape/absorption.
The paper invokes ordinary two-sample t-tests for skewed samples without specifying Welch/pooled variance, independence, effect sizes, intervals, or multiplicity correction.
Results call the 10 dB condition an SNR threshold even though no noise-power model converts link margin into SNR.
The coordinates labeled L.A. fall near San Diego, and Figure 4 visually places the marker there.
Table 5 reports an L.A. maximum of 810.67 km, while the next page says 810.42 km.
The method promises three locations/three simulations but names and reports only Honduras and L.A.
Part III says 1000 trials, the 0-60 degree scan at 0.1 degree supplies 601 settings, and the Letter calls Honduras a 600-ray simulation.
The body calls 30 degrees/3 MHz ideal while the Letter recommends about 10 degrees/20 MHz; bounce and distance objectives are not reconciled.
Part III and Figure 3 specify west, while the Letter says southwest.
Observed first/second-bounce extrema do not prove continuous, stable, or probabilistic reception across 187.67-1622.24 km.
180/190/210 dBm are described as total signal after adding gain and sensitivity, while Figure 16 labels them dB; absolute power, gain, and margin are mixed.
100, 1000, and 100000 W are called order-of-magnitude steps although the last jump is 100-fold and 100 kW practicality is not discussed.
Tables 6-8 repeatedly print Standard Derivation rather than Standard Deviation.
The IRI years are treated as solar-activity levels without isolating season, epoch, or other model-version differences; per-group sample sizes are absent.
Figures 8-9 compare model outputs with model-informed expectations, not measured bounce locations or an independent propagation benchmark.
Figure 9 jumps back to escape probability one near 1e12 electrons/m^3 without sample counts, confidence bands, or physical explanation.
Figures 12-14 do not distinguish zero, no successful sample, all escaped, and all absorbed cells or show uncertainty.
Figure 16 shows similar 190/210 medians and a much wider 210 upper tail; a mean-only monotone conclusion hides heteroscedasticity.
The Letter lacks salutation, recipient, sign-off, or an executable checklist and makes the overstrong claim that skywave is the only non-line-of-sight method.
No code, random seeds, exact IRI query parameters, surface generator settings, or empirical validation dataset are released.

writing_logic.summary: Uses trajectory -> loss -> experiment -> metrics -> operating guidance as a five-paragraph miniature of the paper.
Narrows historical need to skywave communication, decomposes the task, compares method families, proves full-path necessity, and announces selective fidelity.
Defines path outputs before construction so later metrics are not selected after seeing results.
Previews the output contract of propagation and ground modules before equations.
States direction and range expectations before presenting validation plots.
Uses a shared baseline and changes named surface or geographic inputs to make comparisons parallel.
Moves from an arbitrary baseline to a tested working ridge and explicit absorption/escape failure modes.
Turns each omitted dimension into a required data/model extension and finally an empirical comparison protocol.
Reorders the technical chain around an audience problem, controls, range, reliability boundary, and use rather than copying the Summary.
